summary: SPACE QUEST is an interactive, gamified educational web application designed primarily for children aged 8–14. It operates as a virtual space agency where young users step into the role of a Space Mission Commander. Rather than just reading textbooks about space, children actively apply scientific concepts by designing their own spacecraft, balancing real physics constraints, assembling crews, and launching interactive missions across the solar system. The application seamlessly blends a premium, futuristic "mission control" UI with deep educational layers, including an interactive Space Lab for physics simulations and a Space Academy that integrates real-time NASA data.
details:
• What it does and how it works: Users start at a central Mission Control dashboard where they track their Experience Points (XP) and badges. They select a mission (e.g., exploring Mars or Saturn's moons) and enter the Spacecraft Builder. Here, they snap together engines, fuel tanks, and command modules. The app runs real-time physics calculations to ensure the ship has enough thrust, fuel, and power to reach its destination. After passing a "Learn Before You Launch" educational quiz and assigning a crew, users initiate a launch simulation complete with mid-flight problem-solving events. Finally, they explore the destination's surface in a mini-game to collect Science Data.
    • Frontend: React (JavaScript) for the interactive UI, Tailwind CSS for the futuristic glassmorphism styling, and Lucide React for iconography.
    • Backend: Firebase (Authentication & Cloud Firestore) to securely save and sync user profiles, XP, and badges across sessions.
    • External APIs: RESTful API fetching for live NASA open data.
  • How is your project creative? It introduces a "Dual-Mode" learning system. When clicking on a rocket part, users can toggle between "Kids Mode" (simple analogies) and "Explorer Mode" (advanced scientific terminology). It also features ASTRA, an integrated AI-style mentor that monitors the user's spacecraft build and provides contextual engineering warnings (e.g., "Power Failure! You are using more power than you generate.").
  • What factors did your team consider? We heavily prioritized UI/UX for children, ensuring large click targets, clear visual feedback, and vibrant colors. We also considered network reliability by implementing robust try/catch fallbacks for our NASA API fetches—if the API goes down or hits a rate limit, the app gracefully loads offline fallback data so the child's learning experience is never interrupted.
